correctness.rationale: For every n≥4, crown Cr_n=K_{n,n} minus the perfect matching and the source TRDF definition, a positive support must include at least two vertices from each shore. Weight≤5 is impossible because a unique 2-defender would require all vertices on its own shore positive, violating the four-support bound (including n=4). A weight-six witness with a_i,b_j labeled 2 and a_j,b_i labeled 1 for i≠j gives gamma_tR=6. All minimum functions use exactly two 2s on opposite shores: for i≠j the cross 1s are forced; for i=j any p,q≠i provide 1s; count n(n−1)+n(n−1)^2=n²(n−1). Encode removed edges a_p b_q as directed arcs. If every minimum function is destroyed, zero-outdegree set O and zero-indegree set I are disjoint and all I→O arcs deleted. For a=|O|≥1,b=|I|≥1,k=n−a−b, |F|≥ab+k=n−1+(a−1)(b−1). If fewer than n−1 edges deleted these O and I are indeed nonempty. A directed edge 1→2 plus cycle on vertices 3..n removes n−1 edges, leaves each original vertex at least n−2 incident edges, destroys all min functions; edge deletion cannot decrease gamma_tR. Therefore b_tR(Cr_n)=n−1. Independent exhaustive TRDF and deletion-set enumeration n=4,5 reproduces optimizer counts and sharpness, but arbitrary n is proved by directed arc argument.
